guide_enrichment.narrative:
Our view differs from the market only at the margin, and Louisville’s defense explains why we are not more aggressive on Wake Forest. The Cardinals hold the better efficiency profile against both the pass and run, while their ability to prevent scoring opportunities is a particular concern. Wake Forest has converted nine of 10 red-zone trips through two games, but we do not assume that early rate will carry over against a defense that has been much better at keeping opponents from creating those chances.

The case for Wake Forest staying competitive starts with Gio Lopez. He has produced 575 passing yards without an interception while adding 98 yards and two touchdowns on the ground, and Carlos Hernandez already has 253 receiving yards. That gives Wake Forest multiple ways to extend drives, but the other side of the ball limits our confidence: opponents have converted 13 of 27 third downs and scored on every red-zone possession against the Deacons. For us, the market is close enough to our underlying expectation that those competing factors do not create sufficient value at the available price, so we pass.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: We are watching Wake Forest’s scoring-opportunity creation against Louisville’s ability to prevent it. The Deacons’ early red-zone results are encouraging, but Louisville owns the stronger longer-run profile in that phase. The question is whether Lopez’s mobility and connection with Hernandez can produce enough sustained drives against a defense with advantages across the broader efficiency metrics.

recent_game.fact: Wake Forest improved to 2-0 with a 38-36 double-overtime win at Purdue on Sept. 12, 2026.
On fourth-and-15 in the second overtime against Purdue, Gio Lopez completed a 15-yard pass to Carlos Hernandez; Lopez then scored the tying touchdown and winning two-point conversion.
Wake Forest committed no turnovers against Purdue.
Purdue quarterback Ryan Browne passed for 329 yards, and running back Fame Ijeboi rushed 27 times for 114 yards and three touchdowns against Wake Forest.

quarterback.fact: Starting quarterback Gio Lopez has completed 37 of 59 passes for 575 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions through two games.
Lopez has rushed 20 times for 98 yards and two touchdowns through two games.
Against Purdue, Lopez went 16-of-27 for 225 yards and one touchdown while adding a team-high 59 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns.
Lopez transferred to Wake Forest from North Carolina after previously playing at South Alabama under current Wake Forest offensive coordinator Rob Ezell.
Redshirt freshman Steele Pizzella is listed behind Lopez on Wake Forest's unofficial projected depth chart.

offensive_personnel.fact: Wake Forest's unofficial projected offensive line lists Tolu Olajide at left tackle, Clinton Richard at left guard, Will Way at center, Ryan Berger at right guard and Aidan Martin at right tackle.
Center Will Way transferred from Weber State in January 2026 and was selected as one of Wake Forest's six captains.
The projected starting receivers are Carlos Hernandez, Antonio Meeks and Kam Shanks, with Ty Clark III listed as the starting running back.
Wide receiver Antonio Meeks previously played at Louisville.
Ty Clark III has 19 carries for 141 yards and one touchdown through two games, including 105 yards against Akron and a rushing touchdown against Purdue.
Carlos Hernandez had six receptions for 88 yards against Purdue and has 253 receiving yards through two games.

defensive_personnel.fact: Wake Forest's unofficial projected defensive front lists Langston Hardy and Gabe Kirschke at end, Dallas Afalava at defensive tackle and Zach Lohavichan at nose guard.
The projected linebackers are Frank Cusano and Aiden Hall, with Braylon Johnson at the star position.
The projected secondary lists Deuce Blades II and Ashaad Williams at cornerback, Rushaun Tongue at free safety and Davaughn Patterson at strong safety.
Aiden Hall recorded 73 tackles, eight tackles for loss and three passes defended as a starter in 2025.

coaching_changes.fact: Jake Dickert is in his second season as Wake Forest's head coach after being hired on Dec. 18, 2024.
Rob Ezell is Wake Forest's offensive coordinator, Dan Enos is co-offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach, and Jared Kaster coaches the offensive line.
Dyrell Roberts joined Wake Forest as wide receivers coach for the 2026 season after coaching East Carolina's receivers from 2023 through 2025.
Scottie Hazelton is the defensive coordinator, and Freddie Banks is the co-defensive coordinator and safeties coach.
